notes: Apply per modelled month: S = sum of the model's pre-tax rate components (before any tax or rebate). Use jurisdictions[province][fuel]['residential'] for sector 'residential', otherwise ['commercial']; keep a line only if the model sector is in eligibility.sectors, its thresholds pass (null = no limit; when max_demand_kw and max_annual_kwh are both set the line applies if EITHER is met, per O. Reg. 363/16 s.1.1(1)) and effective_date <= as-of date < end_date (when set). Line amount = rate x base: 'pre_tax_subtotal' = S; 'pre_rebate_subtotal' = S as well (same number; marks a tax charged on the bill before a rebate line is deducted); 'energy_charge_subtotal' = pre-tax sum of per-kWh consumption charges only (no fixed/service, demand or rental charges). Lines never compound: PST/RST/QST/ICE are computed on the price excluding GST/HST. With tax = S + sum(sales_tax amounts) - sum(rebate amounts); for eligible Ontario electricity accounts the 23.5% OER exceeds 13% HST, so 'with tax' is below 'without tax'. 'order' is the display/application order (GST/HST, provincial tax, rebates). Commercial results show tax as invoiced; GST/HST registrants can generally recover GST/HST through input tax credits (not modelled). Excluded: income-tested or application-based assistance (e.g. OESP, LEAP, Ontario and Northern Ontario energy tax credits, PEI Island Essentials Benefit, Alberta Energy Rebate, NS YERP claims by landlords, condominiums, mixed-use and commercial-rate accounts); municipal taxes and fees (City of Winnipeg gas and electricity tax, SaskPower/SaskEnergy municipal surcharges, Alberta franchise/access fees); carbon charges and territorial power subsidies (rate components elsewhere); First Nations and diplomatic exemptions; price-triggered per-GJ rebates (Alberta Natural Gas Rebate Program, $0 for October 2026); announced but not in force (NL Churchill River Electricity Rebate); expired (PEI Government Energy Rebate, ended 2026-06-30). Manitoba residential RST depends on heating use (defaults: electricity 7%, gas 1.4% - flagged for review). As of 2026-10-09; confidence per line.

residential.source_note: RST Act C.C.S.M. c. R130 (consolidation current to 2026-10-07): general rate 7% when payable after 2019-06-30 (s.1(1)); gov.mb.ca: 'The 7% Retail Sales Tax (RST) applies to purchases of electricity, piped gas'. RST 'purchase price' excludes GST, the federal fuel charge and municipal taxes on electricity/piped gas (s.1(1)), so the base is the pre-tax subtotal. Source pages: https://www.gov.mb.ca/finance/taxation/electricity.html ; https://web2.gov.mb.ca/laws/statutes/ccsm/r130.php. Default assumes a home NOT heated by electricity: if at least 80% of the electricity heats the purchaser's dwelling and at least 80% of the dwelling can be fully heated by permanently installed electric heat, RST is 1.4% (s.2(1.2)); electricity used only to heat the dwelling is exempt (s.3(36)). The model has no heating-type input - user review.

eligibility.other: Electricity used to heat a building heated solely by electricity is exempt (s.8(1)(n)(ii)) - not modelled.

commercial.source_note: PST Act (consolidation incl. 2025 c 11): s.3(1)(j) tangible personal property 'includes natural or manufactured gas and electricity'; s.5(1) tax at 6% of value; consideration excludes GST (s.3(1)(b)). Source: https://publications.saskatchewan.ca/api/v1/products/779/formats/1196/download. The s.8(1)(n) exemption covers residential dwelling units/farms, heating a building heated solely by electricity, irrigation, non-profit rinks/pools and municipal street lighting - not general commercial use. Value includes the SaskPower municipal surcharge (s.3(1)(n); not modelled). 6% applies to sales on or after 2017-03-23 (SK Information Notice IN 2017-01).
